content.title: How Much Do Coachella Tickets Cost? A Guide to the Massive Music Festival’s Prices, Crowds and More
content.text: Coachella 2026 tickets sold out within roughly a week. Both weekends — General Admission and VIP — are gone, and the official waitlist is closed. For a festival that draws visitors from over 60 countries and expects 125,000 fans each weekend, that kind of demand signals something worth understanding, whether you’re hunting for resale passes or just trying to figure out what drives the frenzy.The Coachella Valley Music and Arts Festival returns to Indio, California, with over 160 artists performing across seven stages and more than 1,100 hours of live music.How Many People Attend Coachella Each Year?Coachella has sold out almost every year since 2010. Last year, the festival drew 125,000 attendees per weekend. The crowd is more varied than the average age suggests. Families, longtime fans and groups of grandparents have all been spotted at the festival.Coachella Music Festival Faces $28,000 Fine After Lana Del Rey’s Set Ends 13 Minutes LateCoachella's Biggest Performances in HistorySome of the biggest performances in Coachella history drew massive audiences on-site and online. Beyoncé’s 2018 “Beychella” headlining set attracted over 100,000 fans in person and a livestream that reached 458,000 simultaneous viewers, making it the most-viewed Coachella performance ever. Harry Styles in 2022 performed in front of an estimated 100,000-person audience. Earlier landmark sets include Prince in 2008, when daily attendance hovered around 51,000, and Daft Punk in 2006.How Much Does Coachella 2026 Cost?A full Coachella experience can range from roughly $800 to more than $2,000 per person, depending on ticket type and extras.Here’s how the main costs break down:General Admission 3-day passes: $549–$649 VIP passes: $1,199–$1,399 Shuttle passes: $130–$180 On-site camping: $150–$400+ Service fees: $50–$100 Festival food and meals: $30–$60 per dayFlights to Indio and hotel stays can add several hundred dollars per person. Beyond tickets, each attendee spends an average of $375 on food, drinks and merchandise at the festival. Ticket sales alone are projected to surpass $120 million this year.How Many Artists Are Performing at Coachella 2026?Over 160 artists will perform across seven stages, with several making their U.S. festival debut. The music spans genres and generations, with more than 1,100 hours of live performances. Sabrina Carpenter, Justin Bieber and Karol G are all headliners in 2026.Past headliners have set a high bar. Prince in 2008 and Radiohead in 2012 delivered career-defining shows. Surprise acts like Drake in 2019 created viral moments fans still discuss.Organizers have scaled logistics to match the crowd: over 100 food and beverage vendors, 55 bars and 1,700 security and medical staff.Can You Still Get Coachella 2026 Tickets?Both GA and VIP passes for Weekend 1 and Weekend 2 are officially sold out. The official waitlist is closed.The only remaining options are Coachella’s AXS resale system or secondary market resellers, where prices run much higher than face value. Fans hoping to attend are advised to monitor the official resale closely and book travel with flexible cancellation options, as last-minute availability is rare.Why Does Coachella Dominate Social Media?Last year, fans shared over 2 million posts and videos under the festival’s official hashtag. For 2026, that number is expected to surpass that.Flower crowns, glitter and oversized hats have become almost as recognizable as the performances themselves. Art installations — towering sculptures and immersive experiences — serve as viral backdrops. Creative festival outfits generate their own wave of content each year.Since its debut in 1999, Coachella has grown into an event that shapes trends in music, fashion and social media. With every ticket claimed and record-breaking attendance expected, 2026 continues that trajectory.
